edges.notes: QEMU targets Linux hosts and kernel facilities for KVM, virtio, and VFIO-class integration per upstream documentation.
QEMU uses the KVM interface on Linux when KVM acceleration is enabled per QEMU documentation.
QEMU provides virtio device models for guests; virtio is the interface contract, QEMU is the VMM.
QEMU can wire vhost backends for virtio datapaths depending on device and configuration.
QEMU assigns devices via VFIO on Linux for passthrough where supported.
Both are VMM-class stacks with different scope (general-purpose emulator vs microVM product); not drop-in substitutes.
libvirt manages QEMU domains and device models as documented; QEMU is the VMM, libvirt is the management layer.
KubeVirt runs QEMU on Linux Kubernetes nodes for VM workloads; QEMU is the VMM, KubeVirt is the Kubernetes integration layer.
Kata Containers uses QEMU on typical Linux VM sandbox paths; QEMU is the VMM, Kata is the OCI runtime integration layer.
